result:
Typecheck, full test suite (617 tests), and lint all pass clean. The implementation is complete:

- **`src/schemas/issue-import.ts`** — `importIssueRowSchema` / `importIssuesSchema` as specified.
- **`src/types/issue.ts`** — `IssueImportResult`.
- **`src/types/event.ts`** — `issues.imported` added to `TaskflowEventMap`.
- **`src/types/activity.ts`** + `activity-labels.ts` — `issues.imported` added as an `ActivityAction`.
- **`src/server/db/schema/issues.ts`** + **`migrate.ts`** — new `issue_imports` table (unique on `org_id, import_key`) so replays survive restarts.
- **`src/server/repositories/issue-import-repository.ts`** — lookup/insert for replay records.
- **`src/server/services/issue-service.ts`** — `importIssues`: same access gates as `createIssue` (tenant scope → project lookup → archived check → permission), replay short-circuit, batch quota check via `wouldExceedLimit(..., rows.length)`, batch rate-limit spend via `consumeRateLimit("issue:create", rows.length)`, then (only after all checks pass) case-insensitive assignee resolution against active members, case-sensitive label get-or-create, sequential numbering continuing from `nextIssueNumber`, one `issues.imported` emit, and a persisted import record.
- **`activity-service.ts`**, **`usage-service.ts`**, **`search-service.ts`** — each now react to `issues.imported` (one audit row, usage meter bump by count, reindex every imported issue); webhook and notification services were deliberately left untouched so imports never trigger deliveries or notifications.

I verified the full flow (creation, numbering continuity, assignee/label resolution, single batch event, replay semantics, quota refusal not burning the key, and access-error mapping) with a temporary test, then removed it.
